user_query: Caller has a criminal matter (arrest, charge, police investigation). How do I triage this?
variations: Caller has been charged in State Courts.
Caller is a foreigner facing a criminal charge.
part_a_general_info: This entry runs after the caller has been routed here from GEN3-T01 Route G. The Criminal Stream is governed primarily by the Criminal Legal Aid Scheme (CLAS), administered by Pro Bono SG. CLAS eligibility: • Caller is a foreigner. • Caller is charged with a non-capital offence (i.e., NOT punishable with death). Capital cases (e.g., murder, drug trafficking above statutory thresholds) will qualify for LASCO (Legal Assistance Scheme for Capital Offences), which is a separate scheme. Caller must already have been charged in court. • Offence is one that CLAS covers (https://www.probono.sg/get-legal-help/legal-representation/). If unsure → escalate. • Caller meets means test (https://www.probono.sg/get-legal-help/legal-representation/), financial documents will need to be submitted upon application. • Caller passes merits test (legal assessment on whether the case warrants representation, this will be done after application is submitted, intern/volunteer taking triaging call is NOT to reject based on their own assessment, no matter how unmeritorious the case appears to be). Singapore Citizens / PRs should be advised to apply to the Public Defender’s Office (PDO) FIRST for criminal legal aid. Only if PDO is unable to assist, does PBSG become the primary route for SGC/PR. PBSG may be able to provide legal guidance and assess suitability for any further assistance, such as representation, on an exceptional basis. Foreigners are not eligible for PDO; CLAS is their first port of call.
triage_questions: Q1: Is the offence a capital offence (punishable with death)?
Q2: Is there a court date/deadline within 14 days?
Q3: Has the caller been charged in court?
Q4: Is the caller a Singapore Citizen or PR?
Q5 (SGC/PR path): Has the caller applied to, or been told about, the Public Defender’s Office (PDO)?

Q6 (Means): Is the caller's Per Capita Household Income (PCHI) ≤ S$1,650, does the caller have savings of ≤ $10,000 if younger than 60 years old (or ≤ $40,000 if 60 years old or older), and does the caller stay in non-private housing (e.g. HDB, shelter, remand/prison)?
branching_logic: Q1: Is the offence a capital offence (punishable with death)?
If Q1 = Yes → Route A (LASCO)
If Q1 = Not Sure → Route F (Escalate to PBSG Staff)
If Q1 = No → Proceed to Q2
Q2: Is there a court date/deadline within 14 days?
If Q2 = Yes → Route D (CLAS + Urgent concurrent — cross-reference GEN3-T06)
If Q2 = No → Proceed to Q3
If Q2 = Not Sure → Route D as precaution.
Q3: Has the caller been charged in court?
If Q3 = Yes → Proceed to Q4
If Q3 = Not Sure → Route F (Escalate to PBSG Staff)
If Q3 = No → Proceed to GEN3-T04 — Civil and Guidance Stream Triage
Q4: Is the caller a Singapore Citizen or PR?
If Q4 = Yes → Proceed to Q5
If Q4 = No (foreigner) → Proceed to Q6
If Q4 = Not Sure → Clarify nationality/residency status; if still unclear, Route F (Escalate to PBSG Staff).
Q5 (SGC/PR path): Has the caller applied to, or been told about, the Public Defender’s Office (PDO)?
If Q5 = No / has not applied → Route B (Refer to PDO First)
If Q5 = Yes, passed PDO or PDO is processing → Route C (PDO is handling — PBSG not needed)
If Q5 = Yes, and PDO is unable to assist → Proceed to GEN3-T04 — Civil and Guidance Stream Triage
If Q5 = Not Sure → Route B and describe PDO.

Q6 (Means): Is the caller's Per Capita Household Income (PCHI) ≤ S$1,650, does the caller have savings of ≤ $10,000 if younger than 60 years old (or ≤ $40,000 if 60 years old or older), and does the caller stay in non-private housing (e.g. HDB, shelter, remand/prison)?
(PCHI = total monthly household income ÷ number of persons in household, including the caller and all dependants.)
If Q6 = Yes → Route E (CLAS — Standard Intake)
If Q6 = No → Proceed to GEN3-T04 — Civil and Guidance Stream Triage
If Q6 = Not Sure → Walk through PCHI calculation live; if still unclear, take down figures and proceed to Route F (Escalate to PBSG Staff).
guardrail: • Under s 33 of the Legal Profession Act 1966, only qualified, practising lawyers may give legal advice. You must NEVER: (a) interpret a legal document for the caller; (b) apply the law to the caller's facts; (c) predict the outcome of a case; (d) tell the caller what they should do legally. • You MAY: (a) confirm scheme eligibility against objective criteria; (b) read out scheme descriptions verbatim; (c) explain PBSG hotline operations; (d) take down particulars and escalate to PBSG Staff. • If the caller insists on legal advice, respond: “I’m an intern/volunteer and I’m not able to give legal advice. What I can do is help you find the right legal help avenue or direct you to a qualified lawyer.” • If in doubt at any point — escalate to PBSG Staff. • Protect caller confidentiality. Do not discuss the caller outside the hotline context. Do not retain personal data on personal devices and/or beyond the PBSG volunteering period.
